exposure: Replacement of the prolapsed umbilical cord into the uterus
Intact survival vs poor neonatal outcome
outcome: Interval between the diagnosis of UCP and delivery
cohort: 267 cases of umbilical cord prolapse (out of 2,037,460 total deliveries) in Japan
finding: Emergency cesarean section and umbilical cord prolapse occurring during labor were associated with a reduction in the rates of poor neonatal outcomes, while a prolapsed amniotic sac, preterm labor, and replacement of the prolapsed umbilical cord into the uterus were associated with increased risk of poor neonatal outcomes.
